findings.title: Adding an abstract method breaks existing OAuth grant provider factories
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is an extension interface, and existing third-party factories compiled against the previous version do not implement `getShortcut()`. The new default encoder's `postInit` unconditionally invokes this method on every installed grant factory, so an existing binary provider causes an `AbstractMethodError` during server initialization; recompiling it also fails until it is changed. Preserve compatibility with a default method or provide a migration path that does not prevent servers with existing custom grants from starting.

findings.title: The public grant context copy constructor was removed
findings.body: The previously available `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` constructor has been removed while adding the grant-type state. Custom grant implementations that copy the request context now fail to compile, and already compiled providers will fail with `NoSuchMethodError` when that path executes after an upgrade. Restore the constructor (including the new `grantType` field in the copy) to avoid breaking provider implementations.

findings.title: Grant shortcut lengths accepted by the encoder cannot be decoded
findings.body: The default encoder concatenates whatever `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` returns, but the decoder rejects every encoded context whose prefix is not exactly six characters. The factory interface documentation currently even describes shortcuts as usually three letters, and the factory performs no two-character validation. A custom grant returning `abc` therefore successfully issues an ID such as `onrtabc:<uuid>`, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` always throws because its context length is seven. Enforce and document an exact two-character shortcut at registration time, or make the encoding self-delimiting/parser support variable lengths.

findings.title: The raw token ID null check validates the grant type a second time
findings.body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. Consequently an `AccessTokenContext` with a null raw ID is accepted, and the default encoder turns it into a literal `...:null` token ID. Multiple invalid contexts can then produce the same JTI and collide with the valid literal raw ID `null`. Check `rawTokenId` here as the error message claims.

findings.title: Access-token event assertions do not validate the expected grant shortcut
findings.body: `isAccessTokenId` reads `substring(3, 5)`, although the grant shortcut in the six-character format occupies indexes 4 and 5, and it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. For example, `onrtac:<uuid>` tested for `ac` extracts `ta`, does not return false, and passes solely because the suffix is a UUID. Thus all updated event tests can pass with an incorrect grant encoding. Compare `substring(4, 6)` and fail when it is not equal to the expected shortcut.
